diagnostic_evidence.quote: Theoretical analysis confirmed the convergence of the RCTZFIF to to the original data-generating function.

issues.failure_explanation: The abstract and conclusion assert that convergence of $\phi_\epsilon$ to $\psi$ (and to the RCTFIF $\phi$) is established. The only supporting result, Theorem thm:convergence, bounds $\|\phi_\epsilon-\psi\|_\infty$ by an expression containing the term $\|\epsilon\|_\infty C\Phi/(1-|\lambda|_\infty)$, where $\|\epsilon\|_\infty=1$ for any nonzero signature and $\Phi=\max|f_j|$ is independent of the mesh size $h$ and of $\lambda$. Hence, for every signature with some $\epsilon_j=1$ (the case of interest, used in all numerical examples), the bound does not tend to zero as $h\to0$ (even with $|\lambda|_\infty\to0$), so no convergence is established by the stated theorem.

failure_location.quote: Rigorous error analysis is presented to establish the convergence of the proposed zipper fractal interpolants to the underlying classical fractal functions, and subsequently, to the data-generating function.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Withdraw the convergence claim and describe the result as an error bound only, or prove a genuinely $h$-dependent estimate for $\|\phi_\epsilon-\phi\|_\infty$ (not supported by the source).
issues.overall_effect: The advertised convergence of RCTZFIFs to the classical fractal function and to $\psi$ is unsupported for all nontrivial signatures; only an $h$-independent error bound is (purportedly) given.
issues.title: Convergence to the data-generating function is claimed but the stated bound does not vanish
issues.why_classification: The honest fix is a limited weakening (error bound instead of convergence); the theorem as a bound survives in form, but the advertised convergence for nonzero signatures is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: a_j = \frac{f_{j+1-\epsilon_j}-f_{j+\epsilon_j}}{y_n - y_1}, b_j = \frac{f_n f_{j+\epsilon_j}-f_1 f_{j+1-\epsilon_j}}{f_n - y_1}.

issues.failure_explanation: The affine map coefficients $a_j,b_j$ are defined in terms of the ordinates $f$ and undefined quantities $y_n,y_1$, so the zipper maps $L_{j,\epsilon}$ are not well defined as written. Taking the intended definition from the endpoint conditions, $a_j=(t_{j+1-\epsilon_j}-t_{j+\epsilon_j})/(t_n-t_1)$ is negative whenever $\epsilon_j=1$; then the requirement $|\lambda_j|<a_j$ (and condition 1 of Theorem thm:positivity, $0\le\lambda_j<\min\{a_i,\dots\}$) is unsatisfiable, making the construction and the positivity theorem vacuous for every reversed subinterval. The numerical section instead uses $|a_j|$ (e.g. $2/15=0.1333$), and the $C^1$ conditions in $V_{j,\epsilon},W_{j,\epsilon}$ require the signed $a_j$, so the correct reading (signed $a_j$ in $d^*$, $|a_j|$ in the constraint) must be reconstructed by the reader.

failure_location.quote: |\lambda_j| < a_j, j\in \mathbb{N}_{n-1}$ is the vertical scaling factor

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define $a_j=(t_{j+1-\epsilon_j}-t_{j+\epsilon_j})/(t_n-t_1)$, $b_j$ accordingly, and replace $|\lambda_j|<a_j$ and $\lambda_j<a_i$ by $|\lambda_j|<|a_j|$, keeping the signed $a_j$ in the derivative conditions.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the RCTZFIF construction admits no valid scaling factor on reversed subintervals and Theorem thm:positivity has an empty hypothesis set for any signature containing a 1, including all signatures used in the experiments.
issues.title: Ill-defined $a_j$ and impossible scaling constraint $|\lambda_j|<a_j$ for reversed (ε_j=1) maps
issues.why_classification: A short local correction of the definitions restores all claims and the intended scope without any new argument.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: If $F_{i,m}(x_n, f_{n,m}) = F_{i+1,m}(x_1, f_{1,m})$ ,$\forall i = 1, \dots, n-2$

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem existence_of_rationalFIF is stated for the classical IFS with orientation-preserving maps $L_i(x_1)=x_i$, $L_i(x_n)=x_{i+1}$ and join conditions $F_{i,m}(x_n,\cdot)=F_{i+1,m}(x_1,\cdot)$. The zipper IFS uses reversed maps for $\epsilon_j=1$ (with $L_{j,\epsilon}(t_1)=t_{j+1}$), so neither the map hypotheses nor the join conditions of the cited theorem apply; the $C^1$ existence of the RCTZFIF is therefore not established by the cited result and requires a separate (standard) fixed-point argument on the $C^1$ space with the zipper junction conditions.

failure_location.quote: By Theorem \ref{existence_of_rationalFIF}, the fixed point of the IFS $\{I\times K; (L_{j,\epsilon}(t), F_{j,\epsilon}(t,f)), j\in \mathbb{N}_{n-1}\}$ will be a graph of a $\mathcal{C}^1-$rational cubic trigonometric Fractal Interpolation Function.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the citation by a direct contraction argument for the Read–Bajraktarević operator on $C^1$ functions with prescribed endpoint values/derivatives under $|\lambda_j|<|a_j|$, or cite a zipper-specific existence theorem.
issues.overall_effect: The well-definedness and $C^1$ regularity of $\phi_\epsilon$, used throughout Sections 4–5, rests on a result invoked outside its hypotheses.
issues.title: Existence/$C^1$-regularity of the zipper interpolant justified by a theorem whose hypotheses do not cover zipper IFS
issues.why_classification: The gap is filled by a routine standard argument; every claim survives unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: Several steps fail. (i) The identity equating $\|\phi_\epsilon-\phi\|_\infty$ with $\sup_t|\lambda_j(\phi_\epsilon-\phi)(t)+M_{j,\epsilon}(t)-M_j(t)|$ uses $\phi_\epsilon(L_{j,\epsilon}(t))$ and $\phi(L_j(t))$, but for $\epsilon_j=1$ the maps $L_{j,\epsilon}\neq L_j$ send $t$ to different points of $I_j$, so the difference is not $\phi_\epsilon-\phi$ evaluated at a common point; moreover $a_j$ has opposite sign in $M_{j,\epsilon}$ and $M_j$, so the $d$-terms do not combine as $a_j(d_{j+\epsilon_j}-d_j)$. (ii) $1/q_{j,\epsilon}(\theta)$ is bounded by $1/\xi$ with $\xi$ defined as a maximum of $q$, which is the wrong direction. (iii) A norm term is subtracted in an upper bound, giving a factor $[\alpha B_1-\delta B_2]$ that may be negative. (iv) $|f_{j+1}-f_j|\le\Phi=\max|f_j|$ and $|d_{j+1}-d_j|\le\eta$ are asserted without justification (false in general), and 'by Theorem thm:rctfif' supplies no such bound. (v) The final constant $C=q_{j,\epsilon}(\theta)/\xi$ depends on $\theta$ and $j$, so the stated bound is not a well-defined constant bound.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must compare $\phi_\epsilon$ and $\phi$ at common points (accounting for orientation reversal and the sign of $a_j$), bound $1/q$ by the minimum of $q$, use correct triangle-inequality signs and difference bounds, and produce a well-defined constant.
issues.overall_effect: The first summand of the bound in Theorem thm:convergence, and hence the theorem's conclusion, is unsupported for any signature with a reversed subinterval; only the cited estimate $\|\phi-\psi\|_\infty$ (Theorem thm:rctfif) remains.
issues.title: Derivation of the bound on $\|\phi_\epsilon-\phi\|_\infty$ in Theorem thm:convergence is invalid
issues.why_classification: The estimate of $\|\phi_\epsilon-\phi\|_\infty$ must be rebuilt from scratch with a different comparison mechanism; no comparable version of the stated bound is supported by the source.
